rationale: The available literature provided in the context does not support the hypothesis that cardiac disease in individuals with the YWHAZ p.Ser230Trp variant is restricted to mild septal defects or pulmonary stenosis without hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. While GeneReviews confirms that classical cardiofaciocutaneous (CFC) syndrome features hypertrophic cardiomyopathy alongside pulmonary valve dysplasia and septal defects, the provided sources referencing Popov-Chang syndrome (OMIM #618428) and YWHAZ only establish associations with epilepsy, brain malformation, and neurodevelopmental delay without providing cohort-level cardiac phenotyping, numerators, or denominators to substantiate the claim that hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is absent.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true prevalence and spectrum of congenital heart defects and cardiomyopathy in all clinically documented individuals harboring pathogenic heterozygous YWHAZ variants?
new_directions.rationale: Direct retrospective or prospective echocardiographic evaluation of published cohorts with YWHAZ variants is necessary to establish whether hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is genuinely absent or simply underreported.

new_directions.question_text: Does 14-3-3-zeta (YWHAZ) p.Ser230Trp expression in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) induce cellular hypertrophy or altered signaling relative to BRAF CFC mutations?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative modeling of YWHAZ gain-of-function versus classical CFC-associated BRAF mutations in cardiomyocytes would directly test the mechanistic predisposition to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
